audits.title: Audit of the dietetic care of patients with type 1 diabetes at a large Australian paediatric tertiary hospital and comparison with the International Society for Paediatric and Adolescent Diabetes nutrition guidelines.
audits.standard: International Society for Paediatric and Adolescent Diabetes (ISPAD) nutrition guideline service delivery targets
audits.setting: Diabetes Outpatient Clinic, Women's and Children's Hospital, Adelaide (paediatric tertiary hospital)

cycle1.result: Newly diagnosed (n = 128): 100% received initial advice from a paediatric diabetes dietitian and 61% had follow-up within one month. More than 1 year post-diagnosis (n = 389): only 6% seen annually.

audits.other_findings: 79% had a condition requiring more frequent review, of whom only 23% were seen more frequently.
audits.citation: Battersby R, Sweeney A, Toome S, Fairchild J, Miller J. Audit of the dietetic care of patients with type 1 diabetes at a large Australian paediatric tertiary hospital and comparison with the International Society for Paediatric and Adolescent Diabetes nutrition guidelines. Nutr Diet. 2017;74(4):408-414. doi:10.1111/1747-0080.12312. PMID: 28901704.

audits.title: Improved clinical practice but continuing service deficiencies following a regional audit of childhood diabetes mellitus.
audits.standard: British Paediatric Association definition of a specialist and national recommendations for childhood diabetes services
audits.setting: Paediatric diabetes services in the south west of England (regional audit)

cycle1.result: 7 of 21 consultant paediatricians met the specialist definition; many children seen in general paediatric clinics; 16 of 21 consultants used glycated haemoglobin.

audits.intervention: Wide distribution of the 1994 audit report to those in a position of influence.

cycle2.result: 12 of 14 consultants met the specialist definition; all centres used designated diabetes clinics; all consultants used glycated haemoglobin.

audits.other_findings: Nursing, dietetic and psychology services remained deficient and paediatric representation on Local Diabetes Service Advisory Groups was patchy.
audits.citation: Drake AJ, Baumer JH. Improved clinical practice but continuing service deficiencies following a regional audit of childhood diabetes mellitus. Arch Dis Child. 2000;82(4):302-304. doi:10.1136/adc.82.4.302. PMID: 10735836.

audits.title: Diabetes care provision and glycaemic control in Northern Ireland: a UK regional audit.
audits.setting: 11 paediatric diabetes clinics in Northern Ireland

cycle1.result: Mean HbA1c 8.8% (SD 1.5%); 20% achieved HbA1c below 7.5%; 76% reviewed by a diabetes specialist nurse and 42% tested for microalbuminuria in the previous year.

audits.other_findings: Better control was associated with attending exactly four clinics a year, Diabetes UK membership and living with both natural parents.
audits.citation: Cardwell CR, Patterson CC, Allen M, Carson DJ, Northern Ireland Paediatric Diabetes Study Group. Diabetes care provision and glycaemic control in Northern Ireland: a UK regional audit. Arch Dis Child. 2005;90(5):468-473. doi:10.1136/adc.2004.061150. PMID: 15851427.

audits.title: Inpatient care for children with diabetes: are standards being met?
audits.standard: Department of Health Children's Diabetes Working Group care standards
audits.setting: 27 children's diabetes services in three regional networks, southern England

cycle1.result: 70% of wards had all four protocols (52% of EDs); trained children's nurses every shift on wards 100% vs EDs 33%; dietetic advice on wards 37%; diabetes team informed within 2 h in daytime 26%.

audits.other_findings: Half of centres reported insulin errors; only 11% would contact the diabetes consultant overnight for PICU/HDU admissions.
audits.citation: Edge J, Ackland FM, Payne S, McAuley A, Hind E, Burren C, et al.. Inpatient care for children with diabetes: are standards being met?. Arch Dis Child. 2012;97(7):599-603. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2011-301212. PMID: 22575715.

audits.title: Auditing paediatric diabetes care and the impact of a specialist nurse trained in paediatric diabetes.
audits.standard: Defined outcome measures for paediatric diabetes care (glycaemic control, growth, annual review, education)
audits.setting: Department of Child Health, University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff

cycle1.result: Only 16% had acceptable glycated haemoglobin; 85% had an annual review (16% background retinopathy, 20% microalbuminuria); before PDSN median stay for new diagnoses 5 days and clinic non-attendance 19%.

audits.intervention: Appointment of a paediatric diabetes specialist nurse.

cycle2.result: Median stay for newly diagnosed patients fell to one day (10 of 24 not admitted); clinic non-attendance fell to 10%.

audits.other_findings: No effect on readmission or length of stay for established diabetes; growth suboptimal after three years.
audits.citation: Cowan FJ, Warner JT, Lowes LM, Riberio JP, Gregory JW. Auditing paediatric diabetes care and the impact of a specialist nurse trained in paediatric diabetes. Arch Dis Child. 1997;77(2):109-114. doi:10.1136/adc.77.2.109. PMID: 9301347.
